title: Venezuelan soldiers 'bled and collapsed' after US deployed powerful sonic weapon during dramatic Maduro capture, according to eyewitness account
description: The United States launched a strike on Venezuela on January 3, capturing President Nicolas Maduro on drug trafficking charges.

title: Following Venezuela, Nicaragua releases prisoners after U.S. demands
description: MEXICO CITY, Jan 10 - Nicaragua's government announced on Saturday that it had freed dozens of people from its national penitentiary system, a day after the United States demanded the release of more than 60 political prisoners in the country. Read more at straitstimes.com.

title: Black Gold or Political Gambit? Inside Washington’s Seizure of Venezuelan Oil And The Future of U.S. Gas Prices
description: This investigation unpacks the geopolitical moves, market realities, and energy economics behind the unfolding story. [USA HERALD] In a dramatic escalation of economic and military pressure, the United States has seized multiple oil tankers linked to Venezuela — some reflagged under foreign registries — as part of an unprecedented campaign to disrupt Caracas’ oil exports A deep dive into the U.S. seizure of Venezuelan oil tankers under the Trump administration, what happens to that oil, and whether American drivers can expect significantly lower gasoline prices.

title: Pygmy on the global stage
description: MORE than 90 percent of highly educated Filipinos will be mightily surprised — and impressed — if at least two of the four highest elected officials of the land — president, vice president, Senate president and speaker of the House of Representatives — can write a coherent essay on how the Eastern Hemisphere in general, and the Philippines in particular, would deftly navigate the aftermath of United States President Donald Trump’s reckless adventurism in Venezuela. Maybe, just maybe, the four can also do this without struggling: locate Venezuela on the map.

title: How reliable is the United States as an ally?
description: FOR decades, the United States has presented itself as the leader and defender of a “rules-based international order” — a system grounded in treaties, institutions, shared norms and predictability. Alliances were framed as moral and legal commitments. Before and even amid the war in Gaza, the “they all come to kiss my ass” trade war, the recent invasion of Venezuela and the seizure of its president, and the massacre of national security guardrails, some allies still tried to insist that the US was a “policeman” of the world. But its recent behavior posed to intelligent minds in every nation, including its allies, these hard questions: Can the US be a reliable ally? Is it even bound by principles, or is it simply a power that acts on something when it’s convenient and withdraws when it’s not?

title: How does the US capture of Maduro affect us?
description: THE United States’ Elite Delta Force launched on Jan. 3 a precision strike on Venezuela that resulted in the capture of its leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores. US President Donald Trump announced their capture and transport to New York to face federal criminal charges, such as drug trafficking and narcoterrorism.

title: Venezuela in talks with US to restore ties
description: CARACAS — Venezuela said Friday it had launched talks with the United States on restoring diplomatic ties, days after US forces deposed Nicolas Maduro as its president.

title: Exclusive-Robert Wilkie: Support Peaceful Protesters in and Out of Iran
description: The historic U.S. mission to extradite Venezuela’s now-former dictator Nicolás Maduro and his wife to United States further isolates one of its primary patrons, the Iranian regime.
